1. **Assess & prepare**: Inventory schema, extensions, custom types, and total size (~2TB); select target managed service (matching Postgres major version); size compute/storage/IOPS for peak load (~4,000 DAU); provision the target instance and configure networking/VPC peering, security groups, and IAM/DB credentials.

2. **Set up replication tooling**: Install and configure logical replication (e.g., pglogical, AWS DMS, or native logical replication/publication-subscription) or physical streaming replication from on-prem to the managed target; validate connectivity and initial snapshot copy mechanics.

3. **Full baseline backup**: Take a full verified backup (pg_dump/pg_basebackup or storage snapshot) of the production database and store it in at least two locations before any further action; confirm restorability with a test restore.

4. **Dry run against non-production data**: Using a copy/clone of production data (anonymized if needed) in a staging environment, execute the full migration procedure end-to-end — initial load, replication catch-up, cutover steps, and rollback — to validate timing, scripts, and tooling; record actual duration against the 2-hour window.

5. **Stakeholder communication (pre-migration)**: Notify all internal teams and the 4,000 DAU user base of the scheduled Sunday maintenance window, expected impact, and fallback contact/status page at least one week in advance, with a reminder 24 hours prior.

6. **Initial bulk data copy (pre-window)**: Ahead of the maintenance window, perform the initial full data load/snapshot copy from on-prem to the cloud target while production remains live, then start logical replication to continuously stream changes and keep the target in near-sync.

7. **Pre-cutover final backup**: Immediately before the maintenance window begins, take a fresh full backup/snapshot of production (post-sync) as the definitive rollback point.

8. **Begin maintenance window — freeze writes**: Put the application into maintenance mode, stop writes to the on-prem database (revoke write access or set read-only), and display the maintenance page to users.

9. **Final sync & cutover**: Allow replication to fully drain/catch up to zero lag, verify no pending WAL/replication backlog, then repoint application connection strings/DNS/secrets to the new managed database and restart application services.

10. **Data integrity verification**: Run row-count comparisons, checksums (e.g., pg_checksums or table-level hash comparisons), and sequence/index validation between source and target for all critical tables; verify application smoke tests pass before reopening traffic.

11. **Go-live or rollback decision**: If verification passes, remove maintenance mode and monitor error rates/performance closely; if verification fails or critical issues arise, execute rollback — repoint application back to the untouched on-prem database (still intact and read-only), restore from the pre-cutover backup if any corruption occurred, and notify stakeholders of the postponement.

12. **Post-migration communication & cleanup**: Announce successful completion (or rollback) to stakeholders and users, monitor the new production system for 24–48 hours, then decommission or archive the on-prem database only after sustained stability is confirmed.

STEP COUNT: 12
